BiblicalUsage: The testimony is the stone tablets God gave Moses, kept inside the ark under the mercy seat, and the word means witness in stone. God tells Moses to put the testimony in the ark, and when the work is done He gives him two tables of testimony written with the finger of God. At the crowning of young Joash, the priest puts the crown on him and gives him the testimony, the written law set over the king as over the people.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe God's testimony is written, not whispered, because He put His words in stone and set them at the centre of His people's worship. I hold that the same written word still testifies to Him today, and I trust it.
